turns.content: hey, thanks for looking at this. i've got cross-correlation data from the reference and probe channels on the underground optical distribution link, and i'm seeing a 28.4 ps transit delay that just appeared at run start. to me that screams physical fiber stretching or maybe a microbend in the conduit—like something shifted during the last maintenance window. i'm leaning toward shutting the link down before the next shot campaign, but i want someone else to validate that read before i pull the trigger. does that number look like fiber damage to you?
I’ll check the data you shared and any prior notes on this link so the 28.4 ps delay is judged against the actual traces, not just a gut read.

yeah so i just pulled the clock diagnostic telemetry from the master oscillator room—actually verified logs, not the raw histograms—and there's a 28.2 ps phase-interpolator wrap in the receiver TDC, unindexed at run start. that's basically the whole differential right there, within 0.2 ps. sooo... does that fully explain the 28.4? or are we still looking at fiber on top of it?
I’ll check prior notes on this link and the delay numbers so we can tell whether the TDC wrap accounts for the whole 28.4 ps.

yeah okay so the clock log definitely lands right on the number, i'll give you that. 28.2 ps wrap, unindexed at run start, appears to account for the differential. but i'm staring at the cross-correlation trace right now and there's a baseline jitter floor around 1.8 ps that was there before run start and it's still there after—does the TDC wrap explain that too? or is that residual something else we need to worry about before i sign off on the campaign?
I’ll check prior notes on this link and the jitter numbers so we can tell whether the wrap is just a static offset or if that 1.8 ps floor is something extra.

ok so you're saying the 1.8 ps jitter floor is resolution-bandwidth limited, not a real timing wander — that makes sense actually, i see it in the raw phase noise plot now. so the whole anomaly was the TDC wrap, nothing physical. i'm gonna hold off on calling the excavation crew then, that saves us like three days of digging and a missed campaign window... but i do need to figure out whether to flag this in the shot review as a known artifact or just let the data stand on its own. what would you do?

Flag it. Don’t let the data stand unannotated.

The physics story is closed: the 28.4 ps “transit” is the unindexed 28.2 ps PI wrap, and the leftover 0.2 ps is just the two diagnostics talking past each other. The 1.8 ps floor is the same RBW-limited hash you already had. Nothing in the conduit moved. Skip the excavation.

What *will* bite you is the next person (or you, three campaigns from now) seeing a 28.4 ps step at run start and spinning up the fiber-damage hypothesis again. Shot review is exactly where that gets killed in one line.

I’d write it as something like:

> Run-start 28.4 ps cross-corr offset is an unindexed receiver-TDC phase-interpolator wrap (clock log: 28.2 ps). Not a fiber/path-length change. Residual ~1.8 ps is resolution-bandwidth limited, not wander. No link intervention.

Two extra things worth doing, not just the note:

1. **Correct it in the timing chain** if that wrap is still sitting in the reduced data. Annotation without a correction means someone will still fit a 28.4 ps delay into a shot timeline.
2. **File a one-line ops follow-up** to index/reset the interpolator at run start so this doesn’t recur. That’s cheaper than another “is the fiber stretched?” thread.

Hold the campaign. Flag the artifact. Fix the wrap in analysis if it hasn’t been applied yet. That’s the clean version.

yeah you're right about flagging it, i'll write it up exactly like that... hold on let me pull up the shot review template. ok so the annotation language you gave is good but should i include the 0.2 ps residual explicitly or just say "consistent with TDC wrap" and move on? trying not to confuse the reviewers with extra noise

Skip the 0.2 ps in the review note.

Reviewers will treat that number as a leftover mystery and you’ll spend the meeting explaining diagnostic agreement instead of the actual conclusion. “Consistent with the TDC wrap” is enough; the clock log already pins it.

Use something like:

> Run-start 28.4 ps cross-corr offset is an unindexed receiver-TDC phase-interpolator wrap (clock log: 28.2 ps). Not a fiber/path-length change. Residual ~1.8 ps is RBW-limited, not wander. No link intervention.

If you want the 0.2 ps on record, put it in the detailed timing log or an appendix, not the shot-review line. That’s the place for “two diagnostics agree to 0.2 ps,” not the one-sentence flag.
